orientation_notes: Plan shape is a 'V'/chevron ('boomerang') mound with two unequal arms (left-hand ride 30-40 m, right-hand ride 50-80 m per S1) meeting at a single apex. Whether the apex points offshore (toward the incident swell) or onshore (toward the beach) could not be conclusively read from the only available plan-view figures (S1 Figures 4 and 7, low-resolution 1999 photocopies with illegible scale bars). This file assumes apex-offshore (the standard configuration for point-break-style chevron surf reefs, and consistent with S1's text describing the fill as 'extending the existing 3 m depth contour offshore' while the arms merge with the natural reef inshore) - flagged low confidence. The reef's overall alongshore axis runs north-south per R2; no source gives which arm is north. Design-era swell assumption (S1): 'predominantly from the west' - no specific compass bearing for the final built structure's orientation was found in any source (Gemini's precise '240-270 deg WSW' figure is unverified/unsourced).
materials: Granite boulders, more than 10,000 tons, individual boulders up to 3 m across, placed on the existing natural limestone reef/bedrock [R1][R2][S1]; two other sources (card's R4/R6) instead describe the placed rock as limestone - unresolved disagreement, carried from the verified card. Volume of rock: 3,500 m3 (Wikipedia, R1) vs ~5,000 m3 (ICM, R4) - also unresolved.

disagree.ours: Perth Artificial Surfing Reef Committee (Balgarnie, Campbell et al.); site selection M. Crawford; sketches by Andrew Pitt; engineering/design by WA Dept of Marine & Harbours and UWA Centre for Water Research (Pattiaratchi, Button, Lyons)

R2 (Gemini's own cited 'Raised Water Research dossier 2024') states 'around 140 meters' (N-S) and '70 meters' (max width) almost verbatim; we re-fetched that exact page directly and it does not contain 115x75 anywhere.
Both R2 ('about 275 meters') and S1 ('250 m') are well above Gemini's 170 m; R2 is again Gemini's own cited source and directly contradicts Gemini's figure.

disagree.gemini: 6200 gross / 5222 net (84% net/gross ratio per Gemini's own audit)
disagree.why_ours: No source publishes an area for Cables, so neither number is truly 'sourced' - but Gemini's own 84% net/gross fill ratio is implausibly high for a thin rubble-mound V built by extending natural-reef depth contours (S1 Figure 4 shows a narrow hatched V, not a filled block); even Gemini's own figures for genuinely broad GSC reefs (Boscombe 59%, Mount Maunganui 51%) are thinner than 84%.

open_issues: Apex-vs-arms orientation (offshore-facing vs onshore-facing V) could not be conclusively read from S1's low-resolution 1999 figures (4 and 7); 'apex offshore' was adopted as a working assumption only - low confidence.

No source publishes a crest width, plan-view footprint area, or exact compass bearing for the arms; the 12 m crest-width assumption and resulting ~2,300 m2 area are this file's own illustrative estimate, not a published figure.

The card's R8 reference attributes the Cable Station design-studies paper to 'Hutt et al.' (from a blocked ResearchGate snippet); the full paper located this pass (S1) lists Charitha Pattiaratchi as sole author on its title page - a likely small attribution correction for the card, not made here (out of this task's scope).
Granite-vs-limestone material naming and the 3,500 m3-vs-5,000 m3 volume disagreement remain unresolved, carried over unchanged from the verified card.

The 250 m (S1, pre-final-design) vs 275 m (R2, final) offshore-distance figures may reflect the card's already-documented mid-construction southern-end extension, but no source explicitly connects the two numbers - an inference, not a confirmed explanation.
